clues.narrowing: Rules out inland and mountain towns; puts the player on the south west shore of a vast river mouth.

source.quote: It is located on the southwest of the Río de la Plata.

clues.text: This city rests on the south west shore of the Río de la Plata, a vast river mouth. Wide water spreads from its port toward the open sea.

clues.narrowing: Rules out steady-climate coasts; keeps hot, wet summers broken by a cold, dry south wind.

source.quote: most heat waves are of short duration (less than a week) and are followed by the passage of the cold, dry Pampero wind which brings violent and intense thunderstorms followed by cooler temperatures.

clues.text: Hot wet summers rule here, till a cold dry wind sweeps in from the south plains. That wind brings wild storms, then cool clear air.

clues.narrowing: Shrinks the list to the port a king made capital of a vast new ruled land.

source.quote: One of his rulings was to split a region from the Viceroyalty of Perú and create instead the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata , with Buenos Aires as the capital.

clues.text: Spain's king split a vast ruled land and made this port its capital. Trade at last could sail straight across the wide sea.

clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one bold partner dance, born in port bars along this river in the 1880s.

source.quote: The tango was born in the impoverished port areas of these countries from a combination of Argentine Milonga, Spanish-Cuban Habanera, and Uruguayan Candombe celebrations.

clues.text: A bold partner dance was born in the poor port areas along this city's great river in the 1880s. Bands played it in port bars, where its mixed steps first took shape.

clues.narrowing: Confirms it: this city has been the seat of the national government since 1880.

source.quote: until the matter was finally settled in 1880 when the city was federalized and became the seat of government, with its mayor appointed by the president.

clues.text: This city is the heart of rule for Argentina, as it has been since 1880. Long past, the chief of the land picked its mayor.

reveal.blurb: Spanish sailors first built a town here in 1536, but attacks drove them off, and a lasting town rose in 1580. The port grew rich on trade, and a king later made it the capital of a vast ruled land. Dockside bars gave the world the tango, and grand streets still draw crowds today. Buenos Aires is the capital of Argentina.
